data.name: Musaddad
data.gender_notes: Musaddad is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root s-d-d which means to fix, establish, or settle. In the Quran, Allah (SWT) refers to Himself as the Firm, Steady one, providing stability and security to His creation. The name Musaddad carries the meaning “Firm, Steady” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Musaddad usually hope their child will grow to embody firm, steady and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes Allah's (SWT) steadfastness and unwavering support.
data.etymology: Musaddad belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Firm, Steady.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Musaddad total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

In the context of Islamic theology, Musaddad refers to a person who is guided by Allah, the Almighty. This name signifies that the individual is on the right path, as ordained by God, and is under His special guidance and care. Historically, this name has been used to denote individuals who have been chosen by God for a specific purpose or mission. The spiritual significance of the name Musaddad lies in its connotation of divine guidance, which is a fundamental aspect of Islamic faith.

historical_references.context: Musaddad ibn Zaid Al-Khuzai was a prominent chief of the Banu Tamim tribe in Basra. He played a key role in the initial Muslim conquests of Iraq and was a supporter of Ali ibn Abi Talib. When Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, the Umayyad caliph, declared war against Ali, Musaddad sided with Ali and led the Banu Tamim forces against the Umayyads. He was eventually killed in the Battle of Siffin in 657 CE.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Baladhuri, Ansab Al-Ashraf, p. 323-324 The name Musaddad carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Musaddad ibn Musafir was a notable scholar and judge in Baghdad during the Abbasid Caliphate. He was born in Kufa and studied under prominent scholars such as Abu Hanifah and Ibrahim An-Nakhai. He gained a reputation for his knowledge of Islamic law and was appointed as a judge in Kufa and later in Baghdad. Musaddad was also a poet and is known for his collection of poetry, which was widely read and appreciated during the Abbasid period.
